newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 100 water tankers will be sent by the government this week to 29 towns and eight cities in and around Manila because of water shortages. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- A Christian group endorses former Senator Aquilino Pimentel to run in next year's presidential elections saying that he is "God's choice." (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Philippine National Police carries out a major reshuffle of officers and men assigned to curb rampant abduction in southern Philippines. (PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- Hundreds of angry Indonesian workers at the Busang mine have taken four people hostage to back demands for severeance pay, news reports reaching Jakarta say. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Foreign chambers of commerce say corporate income tax should be cut to 30 percent from 35 percent under the proposed Philippine Tax Reform Package. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission will widen its investigation of member-brokers of the Philippine Stock Exchange to include those who sold down B shares in anticipation of the declassifcation of common shares. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The sugar industry has formally requested the inter-agency Tariff and Related Matters Committee to retain for three more years the 100 percent out-quota tariff on sugar imports. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
